conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes 'The answer is actually yes, not no' and cites strong trial evidence and WHO guidelines demonstrating that dexamethasone reduces mortality in critically ill COVID-19 patients, directly supporting the claim that it helps more critically ill patients survive.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: The answer is actually yes, not no.** Corticosteroids such as dexamethasone have been shown to reduce mortality in critically ill COVID-19 patients, though they do not guarantee survival for every individual.

**Key Evidence:**

1. **RECOVERY Trial (NEJM, 2020):** The landmark randomized trial found that dexamethasone (6 mg daily for up to 10 days) reduced 28-day mortality by approximately **one-third in ventilated patients** and **one-fifth in patients receiving oxygen only**. Among usual-care patients, mortality was 41% in those ventilated, 25% in those on oxygen, and 13% in those without respiratory support. No benefit was seen in patients not requiring respiratory support. ([https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436); [https://www.recoverytrial.net/results/dexamethasone-results](https://www.recoverytrial.net/results/dexamethasone-results))

2. **WHO REACT Meta-analysis (JAMA, 2020):** Pooling data from seven randomized trials, this meta-analysis found that systemic corticosteroids were associated with **lower 28-day all-cause mortality** among critically ill COVID-19 patients compared to usual care or placebo. ([https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2770279](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2770279))

3. **WHO Clinical Guidance:** Based on moderate-certainty evidence, WHO issued a **strong recommendation** for systemic corticosteroids in patients with severe and critical COVID-19. Corticosteroids remain standard of care due to their effectiveness, accessibility, and low cost. ([https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/who-updates-clinical-care-guidance-with-corticosteroid-recommendations](https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/who-updates-clinical-care-guidance-with-corticosteroid-recommendations))

**Important nuance:** While dexamethasone significantly improves survival odds, it does not "ensure" survival — many critically ill patients still die despite treatment. The benefit is specifically in patients requiring oxygen or ventilation, not in those with milder disease.
